mods.name: CNR Recording Mod
mods.description: Restores the in-game Record button and main-menu Recordings viewer. Replaces the defunct Kamcord SDK with hardware-encoded H.264 MP4 recording via Android MediaCodec + MediaMuxer. Press the in-game Record button to start/stop; tap Recordings on the main menu to browse sessions.

versions.changelog: Fix #5: add Start() to RecordingHook to run button hook on initial MainMenu load (OnLevelWasLoaded misses the first scene)
Fix recordings button doing nothing on main menu: add direct NGUI hook for ShowVideoBtn, bypassing the unreliable Kamcord injection chain entirely
Fix recordings popover rendering behind game UI buttons: set GUI.depth=-100 in OnGUI so the recording list panel and dim overlay always render on top of CNRMod's EcoHook IMGUI buttons
Inject Kamcord.implementation_ in Awake() so the main menu video button opens the recordings viewer
Polished video viewer UI: paginated list (10/page) sorted newest-first, game font time + date per item with size/duration details, detail view with metadata and system player launch
Fix EncodeThread crash: skip releaseOutputBuffer for CODEC_CONFIG buffer (releasing it causes IllegalStateException on c2.android.avc.encoder Android 13); wrap EOS+final-drain in try-catch
Switch capture to Application.CaptureScreenshot per-frame + ConverterCoroutine (PNG->NV12 on main thread); fixes grey frames on WSA/ANGLE where ReadPixels and OnRenderImage see empty DirectX textures
Revive OnRenderImage capture: Kamcord cams disabled so src is actual scene content; fix EncodeThread: sleep 200ms after releasing CODEC_CONFIG buffer to let C2 encoder stabilize

Fix grey frames: disable kamcordPreCamera+kamcordPostCamera during capture (EGL PBuffer redirect stopped), use null-RT ReadPixels; fix EncodeThread: continue after FORMAT_CHANGED (drain pending output), wrap dequeueInputBuffer in try-catch
Fix grey frames: Camera.Render()+targetTexture bypasses Kamcord EGL/PBuffer redirect; fix EncodeThread: sleep 200ms after muxer.start() + try-catch on dequeueOutputBuffer for IllegalStateException
v1.39.12: attach OnRenderImage to Skybox camera (primary scene camera) instead of highest-depth; add src probe diagnostic; add EncodeThread step logging to pinpoint IllegalStateException

Fix grey frames: use OnRenderImage(src,dest) so src is the actual rendered RT instead of the empty GL backbuffer; fix EncodeThread: raw JNI with exact put([B)Ljava/nio/ByteBuffer; signature to bypass Unity 4.6 sbyte[] type-mapping bug
Fix EncodeThread: use ByteBuffer.put(sbyte[]) via JNI instead of Marshal.Copy (fixes IllegalStateException on API 33 caused by corrupt native address)
Fix grey frames: use OnPostRender (fires before eglSwapBuffers) to capture real rendered content; add EncodeThread buffer address logging

Fix grey frames: try null-RT ReadPixels first, fall back to Camera.Render() if grey; fix encoder NoSuchMethodError by removing ByteBuffer.clear() call
false bump for new source code history feature

Fix grey recording: exclude kamcordPreCamera and kamcordPostCamera from the RT redirect. kamcordPostCamera runs last (depth=MaxValue) and its Kamcord native callback overwrites the bound RT with grey. Only redirect real game cameras to captureRT.

Fix grey recording: redirect all game cameras to a captureRT (ReadPixels from RT is reliable on Android). Screen stays visible via depth-1000 CaptureDisplay camera that blits captureRT to screen. ReadPixels from backbuffer always returns grey because Unity renders to an intermediate FBO, not FBO 0.

Fix grey recording: ReadPixels moved to OnPostRender of a depth-1000 no-render camera, which fires after all cameras composite but before eglSwapBuffers. WaitForEndOfFrame was reading the already-cleared new back buffer.

Fix grey recording: drop OnRenderImage/captureRT (only captured Camera.main, which has a grey clear color). Read directly from screen with RenderTexture.active=null in WaitForEndOfFrame so all cameras including NGUI UI are composited. Saves frame0_screen.png diagnostic on first capture.
Diagnostic: auto-record 5 seconds immediately on mod load (main menu) to determine if grey pixels are caused by Kamcord or something else.

Fix grey frames: switch from cam.Render() to OnRenderImage image-effect. Attach a FrameCapture component to Camera.main that blits each rendered frame to our RenderTexture via OnRenderImage � fires inside the camera pipeline before Kamcord's EGL redirect, so src contains real pixels.

Fix grey frames: Kamcord's kamcordPreCamera clears the EGL window surface to grey every frame at game init regardless of recording state. Bypass it by rendering Camera.main directly to our own RenderTexture � Kamcord's EGL pbuffer redirect does not affect FBO-based RenderTextures. Fall back to EGL read if Camera.main is unavailable.

Fix RecordBtnInGame hook: compare enum value by name string instead of hardcoded integer (integer was wrong). Add 5s retry loop so the HUD has time to spawn. Log all UIButtonEventKit button names on first scan for diagnostics.

Root cause fix for grey ReadPixels: stop injecting into Kamcord.implementation_ entirely. The SDK activates kamcordPreCamera on any implementation_ assignment, clearing the EGL surface to grey every frame. Solution: hook the public Kamcord.kamcordDidStartRecording and kamcordDidStopRecording C# events to call StartCapture()/StopCapture(). The existing in-game Start Recording / Stop Recording buttons remain the UI; no implementation_ injection, no overlay button.

Fix grey capture root cause: IsRecording() was returning true (=IsCapturing), which told Kamcord to activate its camera redirect - kamcordPreCamera clears EGL surface to grey each frame and pumps game cameras into an internal pbuffer; since our impl does not perform the blit-back, the EGL surface stays grey and ReadPixels always reads (205,205,205). Fix: IsRecording() now returns false unconditionally. Kamcord camera redirect never activates, game cameras render directly to EGL surface, ReadPixels reads real game content. Start/Stop button calls flow through StartRecording()/StopRecording() directly and are unaffected. Also fix MediaCodecList.getCodecInfos() API (API 21+).

Fix version string stuck at 1.26.0 in log (RecordingModEntry.Version const was never bumped). Restore RenderTexture.active=null before ReadPixels - confirmed correct per v1.22.0: at WaitForEndOfFrame, kamcordPostCamera has already blitted the pbuffer to the EGL window surface; we must read from there. Log which RT was active before nulling it. Query and log the AVC encoder's reported colorFormats so we can confirm what format is actually expected. Yes it expects NV12 YUV (format 21) - the v1.26.0 diagonal grid proved data was flowing through correctly.

Fix grey capture and invalid MP4. Grey fix: remove RenderTexture.active=null before ReadPixels - the game renders into a RenderTexture (Kamcord path) and that RT is the active target at WaitForEndOfFrame; resetting to null caused ReadPixels to read the blank raw backbuffer. MP4 fix: switch from deprecated getInputBuffers/getOutputBuffers (API 21 deprecated, broken on API 36) to single-buffer getInputBuffer(idx)/getOutputBuffer(idx) which return properly-positioned ByteBuffers.

Fix stride mismatch causing diagonal grid artifact and green bar. Capture now writes tightly-packed NV12 (stride=VideoWidth=854, no alignment padding). EncodeThread reads actual encoder stride from getInputFormat (896 on this device) then re-strides each frame row-by-row via Buffer.BlockCopy before feeding to MediaCodec. Encode-side stride is now always what the codec expects.

Fix grey frames definitively: never call MediaCodec during active capture. Phase 1 captures WaitForEndOfFrame+ReadPixels+NV12 frames written to a temp directory on disk. Phase 2 after StopCapture runs MediaCodec+MediaMuxer entirely on a background thread (AndroidJNI.AttachCurrentThread) encoding all saved NV12 frames. EGL context is never touched while ReadPixels is active.

Fix grey frames root cause: MediaCodec.configure/start on the Unity GL thread steals the EGL context, making subsequent ReadPixels read grey. Fix: run all codec init (configure, start, muxer create, prime drain) on a background thread via System.Threading.Thread + AndroidJNI.AttachCurrentThread. WaitForEndOfFrame + ReadPixels stays on Unity main thread. Frame coroutine skips until _codecReady is set by the background thread. _encodingFrame guard prevents coroutine pileup.
Revert to v1.0.0 PNG-frame capture to isolate grey-frame root cause. No MediaCodec/MediaMuxer. WaitForEndOfFrame + ReadPixels + EncodeToPNG. Pixel diagnostic logged on first 3 frames.

Fix grey frames: WaitForEndOfFrame fires AFTER eglSwapBuffers (back buffer destroyed by EGL_BUFFER_DESTROYED introduced when MediaCodec initializes). Switch ReadPixels into OnPostRender of kamcordPostCamera which fires BEFORE the swap while the GL back buffer still contains Kamcord's pbuffer blit. Keep both Kamcord cameras enabled so the blit still happens. Falls back to direct ReadPixels if kamcordPostCamera not found.

Fix grey frames root cause: kamcordPreCamera clears the EGL display surface to grey, then all game cameras render to Kamcord's native pbuffer instead of the display surface. kamcordPostCamera would normally blit the pbuffer back to the display, but our no-op implementation means it never runs, so the screen stays grey. Fix: disable both kamcordPreCamera and kamcordPostCamera at StartCapture so game cameras render directly to the EGL surface. Re-enable them at StopCapture. ReadPixels after WaitForEndOfFrame now reads real game content.

Revert to v1.0.0 capture approach: plain ReadPixels from screen backbuffer after WaitForEndOfFrame, no FrameGrabber/OnRenderImage. Kamcord completely bypasses Unity's RT system at native GL level so all OnRenderImage.src values are grey. The EGL window surface (default framebuffer) has real game content after kamcordPostCamera blits to it, before WaitForEndOfFrame returns. Explicitly set RenderTexture.active=null before ReadPixels to ensure we read from the screen. This is the same approach that produced working PNGs in v1.0.0.

Diagnostic: on recording start, attach a DiagGrabber to every camera that captures one PNG from OnRenderImage.src on the first frame and saves it to /CNRMods/recordings/diag_<CameraName>.png. This shows exactly which camera has real game content vs grey in its render target, so we can pick the right camera for recording.

Fix grey frames: attach FrameGrabber to kamcordPostCamera (depth=MaxFloat) instead of FireCamera (depth=3). Game cameras have empty OnRenderImage.src because Kamcord redirects their GL draw calls to a native pbuffer, leaving Unity's temp RT with just the clear color. kamcordPostCamera is the blit camera whose OnRenderImage.src contains the fully composited frame. Also fixes texture stride bug (GetPixels32 uses _readTex.width as stride, not capW) and adds src/cap dimension diagnostics plus multi-point pixel sampling.

Fix persistent grey frames: Kamcord's kamcordPreCamera redirects all game cameras to render into an internal pbuffer (not the EGL window surface). ReadPixels/OnPostRender always read the window surface which remains grey until kamcordPostCamera blits. Fix: use OnRenderImage instead of OnPostRender. Unity passes src as the actual render target the camera wrote into (the Kamcord pbuffer), so ReadPixels on src gives real game content. Also exposes CapW/CapH for the actual RT dimensions so NV12 scaling is correct even if the RT differs from Screen dimensions.

Fix grey frames: kamcordPostCamera has depth=float.MaxValue so it was being selected as the highest-depth camera, but it clears/overwrites the framebuffer with grey as part of Kamcord post-processing. Fix: skip any camera whose name contains 'kamcord' (case-insensitive) when selecting the capture camera. FireCamera (depth=3) is now selected as the highest real game camera, and OnPostRender on it fires with the fully-composited scene content (Main Camera + Weapon Camera + Camera + FireCamera stacked in depth order).

Fix grey frames: Camera.main is not the last camera to render - the 3D game scene is rendered by a higher-depth camera on top of it. Changed to iterate Camera.allCameras and attach FrameGrabber to the highest-depth camera that renders to screen (targetTexture==null). OnPostRender fires per-camera in depth order so attaching to the deepest screen camera captures the fully-composited frame. Also logs all cameras with their depths and tags at startup for diagnostics.

Fix grey/white frames: ReadPixels after WaitForEndOfFrame reads undefined content on Android because the GLES back buffer has already been submitted to the display by that point. Fix: attach a FrameGrabber MonoBehaviour to Camera.main that captures pixels in OnPostRender, which fires before the buffer swap while the rendered frame is still live. The encode coroutine still yields WaitForEndOfFrame (OnPostRender has already fired by then) and reads the pixels captured by the grabber.

Root cause fix for green frames: ByteBuffer.put(byte[]) is completely unreachable from Unity 4.6 (AndroidJavaObject.Call generates wrong JNI signature "([)Ljava/lang/Object;" for sbyte[] args; raw CallObjectMethod+ConvertToJNIArray throws silent Java exception every frame). Fix: read the native backing pointer from java.nio.Buffer.address (a package-private long field present in all DirectByteBuffers since API 1) via GetFieldID+GetLongField (JNI ignores Java access modifiers), then write the NV12 frame directly into native memory via Marshal.Copy - zero ByteBuffer API involved.

Root cause identified for green frames: ConvertToJNIArray(sbyte[]) was producing a null or wrong-type Java array, causing ByteBuffer.put to throw a silent Java exception (posAfter=0, res=null every frame). Fix: call put(byte[]) via AndroidJavaObject.Call instead of raw CallObjectMethod. ByteBuffer.put(byte[]) is defined directly on ByteBuffer (not inherited from Buffer), so Unity 4.6 resolves it correctly - unlike clear/position/limit which are inherited and always failed. Also adds limit(capacity)+rewind via raw JNI before put to guarantee remaining()=capacity.

Diagnostic + fix attempt for green frames: (1) Switched encoder to COLOR_FormatYUV420SemiPlanar/21 (concrete NV12 format) - on Android SDK 36, COLOR_FormatYUV420Flexible getInputBuffer() may return a stub buffer not backed by real encoder memory. (2) Added Buffer.rewind() before ByteBuffer.put so position is guaranteed 0. (3) Added Buffer.position() log before and after put - posAfter=0 means write silently failed (buffer stays zeroed = green), posAfter=putLen means write worked. (4) Logs NV12 Y[0] and UV[0,1] values to confirm conversion output.

Fix green frames: capture full screen (Screen.width x Screen.height) into ReadPixels texture instead of a fixed 854x480 sub-rect. Scale down to 854x480 using nearest-neighbour integer mapping during the RGB-to-NV12 conversion loop, so the entire game viewport is encoded regardless of device screen resolution.

Fix attempt for green frames: changed ReadPixels capture rect from bottom-left corner (0,0) to the centre of the screen ((Screen.width-VideoWidth)/2, (Screen.height-VideoHeight)/2). On a 2256x1032 device capturing 854x480, the bottom-left 38%x46% of the screen was likely an unrendered or HUD-only region. Also logs actual encoder color-format from getInputFormat() and samples px[BL], px[centre], px[TR] pixel colours in verbose mode so frame content can be verified.

Fixed 0-byte MP4s: queueInputBuffer was throwing IllegalArgumentException (offset=0 size=645120 cap=645078) because getInputFormat() reported stride=896 giving 645120 bytes but the encoder's actual ByteBuffer capacity is slightly less. Now queries real capacity via raw JNI on Buffer.capacity() and clamps both the ByteBuffer.put array and queueInputBuffer size to that value. The 42-byte difference is end-of-UV-plane padding which the encoder ignores.

Fixed crash on record: dropped getInputImage JNI approach (raw AndroidJNI calls on null pointers cause fatal JVM crashes uncatchable by C# try/catch). Reverted to proven getInputBuffer+ByteBuffer.put path. Fixed green frames: query actual encoder row stride from getInputFormat() after codec.start() (typically 864 for 854px due to 16-byte alignment) and write NV12 with correct stride offsets so UV lands at encStride*encSliceH not width*height. Also fixed initialization order bug: muxer and bufferInfo are now created before the prime drain loop so FORMAT_CHANGED can be handled correctly during priming.

Attempted fix: switched to getInputImage+Image.Plane JNI to read actual encoder strides. Caused immediate crash on record button press because raw AndroidJNI calls (GetObjectArrayElement etc.) are fatal when any intermediate pointer is null � not catchable by C# exceptions.

Attempted fix for green frames: switched codec format to COLOR_FormatYUV420SemiPlanar (21) and pixel conversion to NV12. Did not fix green frames because the root issue was row stride alignment, not the format constant.

Fixed corrupt/short MP4s: removed outBuf.Call(position) and outBuf.Call(limit) calls in DrainEncoder � Unity 4.6 AndroidJavaObject cannot resolve these inherited java.nio.Buffer methods on DirectByteBuffer. MediaMuxer.nativeWriteSampleData uses bufferInfo.offset and bufferInfo.size directly so the calls were unnecessary and were crashing the drain loop before any frames were written to the muxer.

Fixed 0-byte MP4s: (1) Removed inBuf.Call(clear) - Unity 4.6 AndroidJavaObject cannot resolve inherited methods on DirectByteBuffer; getInputBuffer already returns a reset buffer. (2) Replaced Unity JNI helper call with raw AndroidJNI.FindClass(java/nio/ByteBuffer)+GetMethodID to find put(byte[]) on the superclass, bypassing the broken inheritance resolution. (3) Always call queueInputBuffer even on write failure so encoder input buffers are never leaked/starved. (4) Added post-start drain loop to capture FORMAT_CHANGED immediately so muxer starts before any frames arrive.

Added verbose diagnostic logging (clears on every boot) to /sdcard/CNRMods/recording.log. Fixed JNI byte-copy: replaced raw AndroidJNI.SetByteArrayRegion (unavailable in this Unity build) with AndroidJavaObject.Call(put, new object[]{byte[]}) which routes through Unity's ConvertToJNIArray. Logs every encode step for first 5 frames and every 60 frames thereafter.

Fixed: 0-byte MP4 files. COLOR_FormatSurface requires the encoder's EGL surface to be bound as the render target, which Unity does not do. Switched to COLOR_FormatYUV420Flexible with dequeueInputBuffer: each frame ReadPixels -> RGBA->I420 conversion -> queueInputBuffer. Hardware H.264 encoder still does compression; CPU cost is ~5-8ms per frame for the colour-space conversion.

Replaced PNG frame capture with hardware-encoded H.264 MP4 via Android MediaCodec + MediaMuxer. Encoding runs on the GPU/hardware encoder � zero ReadPixels overhead. Output is a real .mp4 at 854x480 @ 30fps / 2 Mbps saved to /sdcard/CNRMods/recordings/<timestamp>.mp4. Recordings viewer now lists .mp4 files with file size.

Fixed: recordings viewer window and all IMGUI controls were tiny on high-resolution screens. Applied GUIUtility.ScaleAroundPivot with REF_W=600 virtual-pixel scaling (same as CNRModManager) so the viewer uses consistent physical size at any screen resolution.

Initial release. Injects a custom Kamcord.Implementation via reflection to intercept StartRecording/StopRecording/ShowView. Captures frames at 5fps @ 50% scale (GPU-accelerated RenderTexture blit) and saves as PNG to /sdcard/CNRMods/recordings/<timestamp>/. IMGUI viewer shows session list with frame counts and frame-by-frame preview.

mods.name: CNR Mod (Core)
mods.description: The core mod for Cops N Robbers. Redirects the game to the community LAN server, adds custom map loading, an in-game economy system, and a DLL mod loader that scans /sdcard/CNRMods/ on launch.

versions.changelog: Remove fast visual position prediction to stop side-step rubberbanding and restore stable vertical anchoring while preserving the rotation jitter fix.
Fix fast visual vertical alignment by removing cached body Y offset and clamping jump/fall prediction to prevent players sinking into the floor.
Stabilize fast remote visuals by applying fast body rotation after vanilla updates and adding vertical velocity prediction for smoother jumps and falls.
Fix custom skin overlay layer so second-layer parts follow animated body transforms instead of using a static character clone.
Remove rotation-dependent lateral offset from fast visuals by using vertical-only body/root compensation and avoid late root yaw writes that flicker name tags.
Fix lateral fast-visual offset by using a stable local body offset that rotates with the remote root while keeping vanilla position neutralized.
Prevent vanilla NetPlayerController from fighting fast visuals by neutralizing the next vanilla SetPosition after each fast root apply.
Fix fast-visual drift by converting body-position packets with a stable once-captured root/body offset instead of the live animated body transform.
Fix remote floating by converting fast body-position packets back into prefab root targets with current body/root delta while keeping a single LateUpdate apply pass.
Revert the bad vanilla SetPosition fast-visual path; use one LateUpdate root smoothing pass only to avoid transform feedback drift.
Stop duplicating NetPlayerController body/root compensation in fast visuals; feed filtered body positions into vanilla SetPosition to eliminate diagonal/vertical drift fights.
Fix remote fast-sync diagonal/vertical drift by storing body offset in local space, rotating it with the root, and applying rotation before position compensation.
Stop remote vertical drift/vibration by removing the extra root Y lift and locking vertical position on small flat-ground height deltas.
Add vertical deadzone to fast remote visuals so body-height noise does not appear as up/down vibration while preserving larger jump/stair height changes.
Reduce fast-sync micro-jitter and stop rubber-banding by scaling prediction down near stop, adding a stationary deadzone, and raising the walk threshold slightly.
Add light remote visual smoothing for fast sync: smooth horizontal acceleration, smooth vertical jump motion separately, and cache body/root offset to reduce jump jitter.
Fix fast visual sync payload decoding through the Node Photon relay so event 198 is actually consumed; extend short-term prediction to reduce speed-dependent stepping.
Throttle EcoHook main-menu diagnostics so retry loops do not spam component dumps; keeps lag investigation logs usable.
Reduce multiplayer runtime log spam that could worsen device lag; remove per-packet fast visual sync receive logging and throttle repeated skin/speed diagnostics.
Guard HitReg type lookup to stop invalid Unity FindObjectsOfType calls
Send actual fast visual velocity to reduce remote player stepping
Broadcast skin identity immediately on room entry so reconnects reapply custom skins
Add fast-visual extrapolation so remote players do not freeze between snapshots
Remove fast-visual easing on remote players to eliminate stop-start interpolation
Restore vanilla remote-player fallback while applying fast visual sync at end of frame
Suppress vanilla NetPlayerController on fast-visual remote players to reduce interpolation stutter
Trace fast event reception in the Photon listener and log early packet acceptance so we can confirm whether remote visual sync is actually arriving on device.
Add fast visual sync trace logging for send, receive, and attachment so we can verify whether the remote-update layer is actually active on device.
Tighten fast visual sync by increasing update rate, lowering state age, and reducing animation churn for remote players.

Add fast Photon visual sync on event 198 with 20 Hz local broadcasts, stale packet dropping, and LateUpdate remote overrides to reduce movement, muzzle flash, and animation stutter while keeping vanilla PlayerInfo as fallback.
Add fast Photon visual sync for remote players using event 198 to reduce movement, muzzle flash, and animation stutter without touching vanilla PlayerInfo fallback.

Restore zombie A* pathfinding while keeping vanilla Enemy3 combat and weapon behaviours disabled.
Prevent zombie Enemy3 prefabs from entering vanilla ranged attack AI: keep SingleEnemyAI/enemyLogic disabled and force walk animation during zombie movement.
Hide downed zombie-mode players and disable their colliders on all clients, restoring them on revive or cleanup.
Delay Zombies round countdown until the authoritative host has finished team selection and reached InGame status, while preserving forced Cop team assignment.
Disable local-player overlay cloning to prevent duplicate controller/camera roots while preserving base local skin and remote overlays.
Replace multiplayer mode selection with a fully custom CNR-owned list so vanilla shell modes no longer appear checked alongside CTF or Zombies, and hide zombie HUD outside zombie rooms.
Fix custom room mode radio row ordering by sorting vanilla mode buttons by visual Y position before appending CTF and Zombies.
Fix CTF and Zombies room mode radio buttons appending after the active vanilla mode list without overlapping Stronghold.
Clean stale custom mode rows and remove cloned position tweens so CTF appends after vanilla modes instead of snapping back over Stronghold.
Force CTF and Zombies to sit below the last visible vanilla room-select row using explicit positions instead of sibling-order placement.
Finish the sibling-order placement fix for CTF and Zombies so the custom buttons append after the vanilla list without using hardcoded row offsets.
Make custom room buttons append from the lowest visible vanilla mode row so CTF and Zombies stay below the end of the vanilla list on all maps.
Append custom mode buttons after the last visible vanilla row instead of anchoring them to the hidden Stronghold slot.
Restore CTF to the Stronghold row and place Zombies directly beneath it instead of pushing the stack too low.
Re-anchor custom room buttons to the vanilla mode list so CTF and Zombies stack beneath the visible vanilla rows without adding an extra gap.
Tighten the zombie and CTF room-select spacing so the custom button stack uses the native row gap instead of a doubled offset.
Fix zombie room button placement so it sits below CTF when CTF is visible and reuses the CTF slot only when CTF is absent.
Fix zombie room select to behave like a separate radio option, keep vanilla KC separate, and align the zombie radio button relative to the CTF button.
Integrated zombie mod into CNRMod, added a zombie room option in multiplayer select, and wired the KC-based zombie room flag through the CNR event path.
Sync first-person hand skin material with the equipped player skin so local arms no longer stay on vanilla textures.
Stop truncating skin grid labels and keep DLC preview labels/overlays refreshed across multiple frames so vanilla UI does not wipe them.

versions.changelog: Fix: fireNow now includes FpsOnFire pref (actual WeaponScript touch-fire trigger); add CachePlayerColliders fallback in ScanForLocalBullets
Fix: bullet/knife self-hit - temporarily shield player root (layer 2) on fire so Bullet.Update raycast (mask=19) misses local CC

Fix #8 bullets self-hit (take 3): use CC capsule geometry to distinguish self-bullets from remote bullets. Self-hitting bullets spawn INSIDE the local player's CC capsule (muzzle is inside capsule when firing steeply downward). Remote bullets spawn at the remote player's muzzle -- always outside our CC since two CharacterControllers cannot physically overlap. On detecting a new BulletEnemy whose spawn position is inside our CC capsule (+0.15m tolerance), disable its trigger collider (bc.enabled=false) so OnTriggerEnter never fires. No timer, no fire window, cannot be exploited to dodge incoming damage.

Fix #8 bullets self-hit: Physics.IgnoreCollision has no effect on CharacterController trigger events in old Unity. New approach: during a 0.2s window after firing, newly-seen BulletEnemy instances are local bullets - disable their trigger collider (bc.enabled=false) so BulletEnemy.OnTriggerEnter can never fire. BulletEnemy instances outside the fire window are from remote players and are left untouched so incoming damage still works.

Fix #8 (bullets self-hit, take 2): revert tag change from 3.1.72 (broke weapon pickup/fire). Instead, scan for BulletEnemy instances every frame in LateUpdate and call Physics.IgnoreCollision(bulletCollider, localCC) for each new bullet. All BulletEnemy objects on the local client are the local player's own bullets (remote hits arrive via Photon RPC, not trigger colliders). This prevents BulletEnemy.OnTriggerEnter from ever triggering on the local player's CharacterController without affecting any other game system.

Fix #8 (bullets/knives self-hit): change the local player root's tag from 'Player' to 'Untagged' as soon as the game scene loads. BulletEnemy.OnTriggerEnter and DetonatorForce both gate damage on tag == 'Player' — removing the tag makes all locally-spawned weapon effects pass through the shooter harmlessly. Remote players apply damage via Photon RPC (PlayerDamageOnline) which calls PlayerDamage() directly and never relies on tag checks, so incoming damage from other players is completely unaffected. Hitbox colliders are also disabled (from 3.1.71) for redundant coverage.

Fix #8 (bullets/knives self-hit): disable the local player's hitbox colliders on the local client. Weapon raycasts from this client can no longer hit the shooter's own body. Remote players aim at your remote prefab on their own clients, so incoming damage is completely unaffected.

Fix #8 (snowball / mini cannon physical self-collision): temporarily disable CharacterController.detectCollisions for 0.4 s after each fire event so the locally-spawned projectile cannot be physically blocked by the player's own CharacterController capsule. Also extend the fire-pitch clamp (previously wide-cam only) to all camera modes, preventing raycast weapons (bullets, knives) from self-hitting even when wide-cam is disabled.

Fix #8: prevent projectile self-hits. After any fire event, newly-spawned Rigidbody objects (grenades, RPG rockets) are found and Physics.IgnoreCollision is called between them and the local player's colliders, so the shooter can never be hit by their own projectile in either normal or wide-camera mode.

Fixed: fire button requires two fingers to activate. Root cause: UICamera.useMouse was forced to true on every frame, causing UICamera.ProcessMouse() to run alongside ProcessTouches() on Android. On Android, Unity's simulateMouseWithTouches maps touch[0] to mouse button 0, so ProcessMouse routed NGUI events to whatever widget was under touch[0]. When touch[0] was the fire button this NGUI processing interfered with JoyStickController's Physics.Raycast-based fire detection, causing one-finger fire to fail. With a second non-fire touch held (touch[0] elsewhere) the interference didn't hit the fire button, which is why two-finger fire still worked. Fix: useMouse is now only set to true when KBM mode is active and the cursor is visible (not locked). In all other states useMouse stays false (Android default), letting fire detection work with a single touch as intended.
Reverted 2.0.8 camera-expansion removal (that change did not address the root cause of fire issues). Restores 2.0.7 behavior while investigation continues.

Fixed fire button broken even at default button positions. Root cause: CNRSettingsMod 2.0.5 expanded the NGUI camera viewport to full screen, which changed the camera aspect ratio and shifted all Physics.Raycast hit zones � JoyStickController's fire-button raycast missed every time. The remap introduced in 2.0.6 to compensate had an accumulation bug (positions drifted further wrong on every scene reload), so even 'Reset All HUD' didn't fix it. Fix: the camera viewport is no longer expanded. JoyStickController now works correctly at all default and right-side button positions. The supplemental screen-space fire detector (TouchFireDetect) is still present but now only activates when the fire button has been explicitly dragged outside the camera viewport. Migration: on first run, any button positions saved under the expanded-camera versions (2.0.5�2.0.7) are automatically cleared so the game defaults are used.

Fixed fire button not working when the fire button is repositioned to the left side of the screen. Root cause: after the NGUI camera viewport was expanded to full-screen (2.0.5), JoyStickController's Physics.Raycast missed the fire button, so it reset PlayerLogic.mStatus to 'walk' every frame. The 2.0.6 fallback worked but couldn't persist the 'fire' state because JoyStickController overwrote it the very next Update(). Fix: the supplemental touch detector now also sets JoyStickController's private fireStatusHoldTimeCount field (via reflection) to 0.235f on each detected fire touch. This is the same mechanism JoyStickController uses internally to guard against walk resets � when holdCount > 0 its 'if (!flag && holdCount <= 0) mStatus = walk' branch is skipped, so mStatus stays 'fire' until consumed by the gun script. Cooldown is 0.2f (slightly below 0.235f) so holdCount is refreshed before it ever reaches zero while the button is held.

Fixed firing/aiming issues introduced by the 2.0.5 camera viewport expansion. Expanding the NGUI camera rect changes the camera aspect ratio, which shifts the fire button's Physics.Raycast hit zone away from its visual, causing fire to fail on the first touch and joystick touches to hit the fire collider accidentally. Fix 1 (remap): when the camera rect is expanded, each button's world position is recalculated so it projects to the exact same screen pixel as before � keeping Physics.Raycast aligned with the visual. The corrected positions are persisted so future loads need no remap. Fix 2 (fallback): a supplemental screen-space fire detector runs in LateUpdate; if any touch falls inside the fire button's projected screen bounds it directly sets the fire status, bypassing Physics.Raycast entirely as a safety net.

Fixed: HUD buttons moved to the left side of the screen with the drag editor did not respond to touches at their new position. Root cause: the game's NGUI HUD camera had its viewport rect restricted to the right portion of the screen (the virtual joystick area on the left uses a separate input system and never needed NGUI). UICamera.Raycast() rejects any touch whose ScreenToViewportPoint result falls outside [0,1], so left-side touches were silently skipped. Fix: CNRSettingsMod now expands the NGUI camera viewport to the full screen (0,0,1,1) after applying saved HUD positions, making all repositioned buttons respond correctly regardless of where they are dragged.

Fixed: equipping/unequipping weapons on the profile screen would immediately reverse itself. Root cause: UICamera.useMouse was being forced true globally (including in the main menu/profile scene), causing NGUI to fire extra OnClick events on profile buttons. useMouse is now only forced in in-game scenes where KBM input is active.

Fixed: Link Device result never appeared in the Account tab. The result was being written to EconomyHook._ecoAccountMsg (CNRMod-internal) and never reaching CNRSettingsMod's display. Now polls EconomyHook.ClaimResultMsg via reflection and copies it to the Account tab message field.

Account tab updated: Set Recovery Credentials now requires both a password (6+ chars) and a PIN (4-8 digits). Link Device (formerly Transfer Account) now requires name, password, and PIN matching the new auth scheme.
Full HUD drag-and-resize for all UI elements. KBM bindings with capture mode. ADS multiplier. Wide camera toggle (35deg / 70deg). Account PIN system.
